definition.interpretation: The experiment yielded a preference variance of 0.094, satisfying the predicate variance <= 0.1. This supports the hypothesis that locally-linear learning formulations lead to bounded variance in preference convergence under constrained initial conditions.
definition.limitations: The simulation used a limited trial size (50) and a simple Gaussian distribution; results may not generalize to non-linear or high-dimensional preference spaces.
definition.next_step: Replicate the experiment with increased trial counts (e.g., 500) and broader parameter initialization ranges to test the robustness of the bounded variance finding.

definition.reason: The successful (though limited) validation of the bounded variance hypothesis requires testing with increased trials to reduce potential sample bias.
definition.stop: Variance exceeds 0.1 tolerance or convergence becomes computationally unstable.
definition.uncertainty: It is unclear if the bounded variance persists when the initial hyper-volume is expanded or when the learning process involves non-linear components.
